<page>
Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance
Bodily Injury Unit
Claim Notes
Claim number:
C-1245
Claimant:
Lisa Patterson
Adjuster:
Christopher Wong
1-14-25
Claim opened after a low-speed head-on collision repotred by the insured's driver, who is named on the policy. The
claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact will be routed through the attorney's office.
3-1-25
Police report and two independent witnesses confirm the claimant was seated in the vehicle at the time of impact.
The other driver gave a statement that matches the sequence described at first notice.
3-2-25
Photographs of both vehicles were reviewed. The damage pattern is consistent with the reported impact, and the
front-end deformation lines up across both cars.
4-7-25
Vehicle inspection completed. No prior damage to the affected areas is known from the claim file or the vehicle
history, and nothing sugegsts any of the damage predates the policy's coverage start.
4-27-25
Claimant reported neck pain and stiffness at the first medical visit. The reported injury is a common result of the kind
and force of this type of collision.
5-5-25
Medical records received. Treatment followed a usual course, with physical therapy and a short run of medication,
and the claimant's symptoms eased steadily as they improved.
5-18-25
Attorney's office confirmed the claimant's account. The claimant has given the same description of events in every
conversation so far, including the initial call, the recorded statement, and the follow-up interview.
7-19-25
Reviewed prior medical history with the claimant's authorization. No earlier injury to the neck or upper back is
documented, and no prior claims involving the same body area appear in the index search.
7-31-25
Treating provider's notes show progressive improvement with reduced visit frequency over the following weeks. The
treatment timeline is in line with a typical soft-tissue recovery.
8-19-25
Witness statements, photographs, and the other driver's account all confirm the collision occurred as described. No
conflicting information has been found in the file.
8-21-25
Claim reviewed against all available documentation. The injury, treatment course, vehicle damage, and account of
events are consistent with one another, and the file is ready for settlement evaluation with counsel.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- occurrence_support: Do independent sources (witnesses, photos, cameras, the other driver) confirm that the accident happened as described? Allowed: Confirmed, Partially corroborated, Uncorroborated, Contradicted, Suspected staged.
- damage_crash_fit: Does the vehicle damage fit the described impact? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- account_stability: Did the claimant's account of the accident stay the same over time? Allowed: Stable, Clarified, Materially changed.
- occupant_presence: Was the claimant really in the vehicle at the time of the crash? Allowed: Verified, Unclear, Added later, Not present.
- prior_damage_evidence: Is there evidence of vehicle damage from before this crash? Allowed: None, Possible, Documented, Material.
- known_loss_evidence: Is there evidence the damage existed or was known before the coverage started? Allowed: Weak, Moderate, Strong.
- driver_status: Is the driver of the insured vehicle on the policy? Allowed: Listed, Household, Unlisted, Excluded.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
